data.finding: Isolated mTOR as the FKBP12-rapamycin-associated protein controlling G1-S progression.
data.abstract_excerpt: The immunosuppressive drug, rapamycin, interferes with an undefined signaling pathway required for the progression of G1-phase T-cells into S phase. Genetic analyses in yeast indicate that binding of rapamycin to its intracellular receptor, FKBP12, generates a toxic complex that inhibits cell growth in G1 phase. These analyses implicated two related proteins, TOR1 and TOR2, as targets of the FKBP12-rapamycin complex in yeast.

extracted_findings.effect: Isolation of the mammalian FKBP12-rapamycin target protein (mTOR)
